user.title: MQTT Actions
user.description: Set up MQTT Actions for this Home Assistant instance. All instances that share devices must use the same base topic.

data_description.base_topic: Root of all topics used by MQTT Actions, for example mqtt_actions. It is written into retained messages on the broker and cannot be changed later. To use another base topic, remove this integration and set it up again.
data_description.instance_name: Name of this Home Assistant instance.

error.invalid_base_topic: The base topic must not be empty, must not contain # or +, must not start or end with a slash, must not contain empty levels, and must not start with $.
error.instance_name_required: The instance name must not be empty.
error.instance_name_invalid: The instance name must be printable and at most 64 characters long.

abort.mqtt_required: The MQTT integration must be set up first.
abort.single_instance_allowed: MQTT Actions is already set up. Only one hub per Home Assistant instance is allowed.

user.title: Add switch device
user.description: The actions run when the state topic of this device changes to ON or OFF.

data_description.name: Name of the switch entity that is created.
data_description.on_change_to_on: Runs on this instance when the state changes to ON. Prefer entity, area or label targets: device IDs differ between Home Assistant instances.
data_description.on_change_to_off: Runs on this instance when the state changes to OFF. Prefer entity, area or label targets: device IDs differ between Home Assistant instances.
data_description.run_on_startup: When enabled, the retained state is treated as a change once after Home Assistant starts or the integration reloads, so the matching actions run even if the state has not changed.
data_description.run_mode: Serial queues runs and executes them one after another. Restart cancels the running actions when a new change arrives.
data_description.breaker_max_runs: The circuit breaker pauses the device when it would run its actions more often than this within the window. Releasing means changing the device or reloading the integration. Whole number from 1 to 100.
data_description.breaker_window: Length of the circuit breaker window in seconds. Whole number from 1 to 3600.

delete_device.title: Delete the device?
delete_device.description: Delete the device {name}? It is removed on all connected instances, not only on this one. Other instances currently online: {count}. They lose the device as well, and instances that are offline lose it as soon as they are connected again. The retained configuration, discovery and state of the device are deleted from the broker. This cannot be undone.

menu_options.delete_confirmed: Yes, delete the device on all instances

error.name_invalid: The name must be printable and at most 64 characters long.

menu.title: Options

add_option.title: Add option
add_option.description: The state value is the text that arrives on the state topic. It cannot be changed after the option exists. The friendly name is what the select entity shows.

data_description.state_value: Exact text of the state topic payload for this option, without spaces at the start or end. Payloads are matched ignoring case.
data_description.friendly_name: Name of the option in the select entity. It must be different for every option and cannot be none.
data_description.actions: Runs on this instance when the state changes to this option. Optional. Prefer entity, area or label targets: device IDs differ between Home Assistant instances.

edit_option.title: Edit an option
edit_option.description: Choose the option to edit. Its state value cannot be changed.

edit_option_details.title: Edit option
edit_option_details.description: State value: {state_value}. The state value cannot be changed. If this option is the one currently selected, the entity shows unknown after you rename it, until the next valid state message arrives.

data_description.friendly_name: Name of the option in the select entity. It must be different for every option and cannot be none.
data_description.actions: Runs on this instance when the state changes to this option. Optional. Prefer entity, area or label targets: device IDs differ between Home Assistant instances.

remove_option.title: Remove an option
remove_option.description: Choose the option to remove. You confirm the removal on the next page.

remove_confirm.title: Remove the option?
remove_confirm.description: Remove the option {friendly_name} with the state value {state_value}? Messages with this state value are ignored and logged afterwards. If this option is currently selected, the entity shows unknown until the next valid state message arrives. The change is saved when you choose Save the device.

This cannot be undone.

init.title: MQTT Actions options
init.description: Choose what happens to your devices when you remove this integration. The choice is read at the moment of removal, so set it before you remove the integration.

data.delete_devices_on_remove: Delete all devices when this integration is removed

data_description.delete_devices_on_remove: Off by default: removing this integration leaves all its devices and their retained messages on the broker, and other instances keep them as orphans that show as unavailable. On: removing this integration deletes all devices created on this instance from the broker and from every connected instance.

action_failed.title: An action failed
action_failed.description: The actions for {trigger} of {device} failed at {time}: {error}

mqtt_discovery_disabled.title: MQTT discovery is disabled
mqtt_discovery_disabled.description: MQTT Actions creates its entities through MQTT discovery, but discovery is disabled in the MQTT integration. No entity of MQTT Actions appears until discovery is enabled again in the MQTT integration options.

circuit_breaker_tripped.title: A device was paused by the circuit breaker
circuit_breaker_tripped.description: {device} ran its actions more than {max_runs} times within {window} seconds. This usually means an action changes the state of its own device and keeps triggering itself, so MQTT Actions stopped the running actions and paused the device. Changes on the state topic still update the entity, but no actions run until the device is released. To release it, change the settings of the device or reload the integration. Saving the device without changing anything does not release it.

doc_overwritten.title: The shared configuration of a device was overwritten
doc_overwritten.description: Something other than this instance changed or cleared the shared configuration of {device} on the MQTT broker. This instance is the owner of {device}, so it published its own configuration again. Check who can write to the topics of MQTT Actions on the broker and restrict write access to the owning instance.

ownership_claim.title: Another instance claims a device that you own
ownership_claim.description: The instance {claimant} published a configuration for {device}, which is owned by this instance. This instance remains the owner and published its own configuration again. There is no takeover: only the owner can edit or delete a device.

discovery_removed.title: The entities of a device were removed repeatedly
discovery_removed.description: The entities of {device} were removed {count} times recently, for example by deleting an entity on another Home Assistant instance. Each time, this instance published the discovery again. Deleting an entity on one instance removes it on every instance, so delete the device itself if you no longer want it.

owner_conflict.title: Another instance claims a device that you follow
owner_conflict.description: The device {device} is owned by {owner}. Another instance named {claimant} also published a configuration for it. This instance keeps following {owner} and ignores the other claim. Check the access rights of the instances on the MQTT broker, so that each instance can only write its own devices.

schema_too_new.title: A shared device configuration needs a newer integration
schema_too_new.description: The shared configuration of {device} uses format version {version}, but this integration understands up to version {supported}. The device keeps its last known settings. Update MQTT Actions on this instance to receive changes.

approval_required.title: A device from another instance wants to run actions here
approval_required.description: The device {device} from {owner} wants to run actions on this instance (hash prefix {hash}). The actions do not run until you approve them. Open this repair to review them.

confirm.title: Approve the actions of a device from another instance
confirm.description:
You are about to approve the device **{device}** from the instance **{owner}**.

The actions below run on this Home Assistant instance, with its full access, whenever the state of the device changes. If run on startup is true, they also run on the first state received after every start of Home Assistant, every reload of the integration and every reconnect to the broker.

Run on startup: **{startup}**

Run mode: **{run_mode}**. The circuit breaker pauses the device after more than **{breaker_max_runs}** runs within **{breaker_window}** seconds. The run mode and both limits are part of this approval, and a change of any of them asks for approval again.

```yaml
{actions}
```

Templated service names (the real service is only known when the action runs):

{templated}

Steps that call scripts, automations, scenes, buttons, device actions or events, or turn something on or off generically (these are not restricted):

{residual}

Triggers whose actions do not validate on this instance:

{invalid}

This approval is bound to the hash {hash}. It lapses when the owner changes the actions, and you are asked again. Nothing runs until you submit.

abort.changed: The actions changed while this dialog was open, so nothing was approved. Open the new request in Repairs to review the changed actions.
abort.too_large: The actions are too long to review here, so nothing was approved and the device stays paused.
abort.not_loaded: MQTT Actions is not loaded, so nothing can be approved. Try again when the integration is running.

mirror_blocked.title: A device from another instance is blocked
mirror_blocked.description: The device {device} from {owner} uses services that are never allowed for actions received from other instances ({services}). It is paused and cannot be approved. Ask the owner to remove these services from the device.

denied_service_call.title: An action from another instance was stopped
denied_service_call.description: A run of {trigger} of {device} was stopped because a templated service name resolved to the forbidden service {service}. Actions received from other instances may never call this service.

resync.name: Resync
resync.description: Publishes everything this instance owns to the broker again: the config documents, the discovery and the online status. A second call within a few seconds is refused.

export_devices.name: Export devices
export_devices.description: Returns the devices this instance owns as a JSON document, and optionally writes the document to a private file in the mqtt_actions folder of the configuration directory. The export holds the actions and no device ids, so an import always creates new devices. Devices mirrored from other instances are never exported.

device_id.name: Devices
device_id.description: The devices to export. Leave empty to export all devices of this instance.

file_name.name: File name
file_name.description: Also write the export to this file in the mqtt_actions folder of the configuration directory. Letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore only, ending in .json, at most 64 characters before the extension.

not_loaded.message: MQTT Actions is not loaded. Check that the integration is set up and that MQTT is available.

resync_throttled.message: A resync just ran. Wait a few seconds and try again.

unknown_device.message: This device does not exist in the device registry.

not_a_device.message: This is not a device of MQTT Actions. Pick the device of a Switch or Select.

export_not_owned.message: Only devices owned by this instance can be used here. A mirror of another instance cannot.

bad_file_name.message: The file name is not allowed. Use letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore only, start with a letter or digit, end in .json and keep it to 64 characters before the extension.

export_write_failed.message: The export file could not be written. See the Home Assistant log for the reason.
